members.name: persuasion_v5e_a
members.instructions: {"task": "In a chat where a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate to Save the Children, tag the persuader message after 'Persuader message to tag:' with the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses. Use the earlier dialogue only as context; tag only the final message.", "guidance": ["Pick the option that best describes the main act of the tagged message.", "Statements about the charity are credibility; statements about donation mechanics are donation information; statements about children's suffering are emotion.", "Questions are inquiries unless they ask the persuadee to donate (proposition) or ask how much (ask amount)."]}

criteria.credibility_org_facts: Describes or praises Save the Children itself: what it is, what it does, where it works, its programs, history, founder, reach, reputation, ratings, trustworthiness, how funds are spent (e.g. '86% goes to programs'), or answers the persuadee's question about the charity. Also pointing to the charity's website or a URL for more information.
criteria.credibility_tackling_suffering: Describes a problem children face framed as what the charity is doing about it (e.g. 'They are helping children at the border reunite with parents').
criteria.emotion_suffering: Evokes feelings (sadness, sympathy, guilt, hope) about children's suffering: describes hardship, deaths, war, hunger, children needing help, the persuader imagining their own child suffering ('I have a son and can't imagine seeing him hungry'), a story or sad anecdote about a child or person who suffered (e.g. the story of Bruce, 'a friend lost a child to hunger'), or the persuader's own sadness about it (e.g. '1,000 children were killed in Syria', 'It makes me so sad', 'The children need you!').
criteria.logical_effect: Reasons that a donation has a real effect or impact ('your donation will make a big difference', 'it will go to good use', donations are matched so every amount is doubled), benefits to the donor ('you could feel great about helping those kids'), moral reasoning ('children are the future', 'everyone deserves a chance', 'we should all pitch in'), or cost arguments ('skip a cup of coffee and donate it', 'if everyone gave a nickel...', '$2 you won't miss', 'you are donating money you don't even have yet, so you won't miss it').
criteria.foot_in_door_small_helps: Argues that even a small amount helps or makes a difference: 'every little bit helps', 'even the smallest donation makes a difference', 'a tiny amount can go a long way', 'any amount we collect is welcome'. Merely stating what amounts are allowed ('you can donate as little as 1 cent and as much as 2 dollars', 'it can be as much as you want') is donation information instead.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader says they themselves donate, will donate, or will match the persuadee's donation ('I will also give money today', 'I donate to them regularly', 'I'll match your donation').
criteria.personal_story: The persuader tells about their own first-hand experience of giving or helping ('I worked in Africa and saw what a few dollars can do'). Narrating the story of a child in need (e.g. Bruce) or a sad anecdote about someone suffering is emotion appeal instead.
criteria.donation_information: Explains how donating works in this task or in general: the donation is deducted from the task payment, the research team collects and sends it, what amounts are allowed ('anywhere from $0 to your full payment', 'as little as 1 cent and as much as 2 dollars', 'it can be as much as you want'), when or how to donate, payment methods, or a suggested amount ('I would suggest $20 a month').
criteria.source_inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of Save the Children or what they know about the organization ('Have you heard of Save the Children?', 'Are you familiar with them?').
criteria.task_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's opinions or habits regarding donating, charity, or the cause ('Do you donate to charities?', 'What do you think?', 'Do you believe children deserve help?', 'Did you know 16,000 children die each day?'), or offers to answer the persuadee's questions or give more information ('Is there any information I could provide you with?', 'What questions do you have?').
criteria.personal_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's personal life unrelated to donating ('Do you have children?', 'Where are you from?', 'Tell me about your life').
criteria.greeting: Hello/hi, 'how are you?', 'nice to meet you', or replying to 'how are you' ('I'm doing well, thank you', 'how about you?').
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee ('Thank you for your time and donation', 'We appreciate your help').
criteria.proposition: Asks or urges the persuadee themselves to donate, without asking for an amount (asking them to tell friends or spread the word is not this) ('Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?', 'Would you consider donating?', 'We should donate to them!', 'Now I would like to ask you to donate').
criteria.ask_amount: Asks how much the persuadee will donate, or asks if they could give a specific amount ('How much would you like to give?', 'What amount are you comfortable with?', 'could you afford fifteen cents?').
criteria.praise_user: Praises the persuadee: compliments them as a person ('You are a very kind person', 'People like you make the world better') or praises their generosity, kindness or willingness to donate ('That is very generous.', 'It is wonderful that you are willing to donate!', 'I admire that!'). A bare exclamation with no praise of the person ('Great!', 'Awesome!', 'That's amazing!') is acknowledgement instead.
criteria.acknowledgement: Clearly agrees with or reacts positively to what the persuadee just said ('I agree 100%', 'That's great to hear', 'Great!', 'Awesome!', 'That's amazing!', 'Yes they do', 'Me too', 'I understand', 'That makes sense'), without praising the persuadee's generosity.
criteria.other_filler: Flat fillers with little content: 'Ok...', 'Fine...', 'Yeah.', 'yes, indeed.'
criteria.other_answer: Answers a question the persuadee asked about the persuader or the conversation ('Yes, I'm familiar with them', 'I'm not sure'), clarifies something ('Half of 1 dollar?'), or states the persuader's own role in the conversation ('I am volunteering for the charity called Save the Children', 'I'm working for this organization').
criteria.other_confirm_or_more: Confirms the amount the persuadee will donate ('So you are donating $10, right?') asks them to donate a bit more, or asks them to get friends and family to help or spread the word.
criteria.other_closing: Closing remarks and farewells ('Have a great day!', 'Take care').
criteria.other_smalltalk: Small talk or chit-chat not about the charity or donating ('North Carolina is nice', 'Bucket lists are good'), or anything that fits no category.
criteria.off_task: Talks about the HIT/survey/chat logistics or is completely unrelated or nonsense ('we need 10 chats each to complete this hit', 'Stupid').
